# 2026-07-26 · Rotating refresh tokens

Change ID: `rotating-refresh-tokens`
Created: `2026-07-26T10:00:00+00:00`
Risk: R3
Status: In progress

## Problem and intended outcome

Refresh tokens were issued once and stayed valid until someone noticed a leak
and revoked it by hand. `is_refresh_valid` had no way to tell a legitimate
token from a stolen copy of it, so a leaked 90-day token was usable by an
attacker for up to 90 days unless a human intervened.

The intended outcome is that every refresh exchanges the presented token for
a new one (rotation), and that presenting a token that has already been
exchanged — the signature of a stolen copy being used in parallel with the
legitimate one — revokes the entire session rather than just failing that one
request.

## Success and non-goals

Success is that a stolen refresh token becomes useless the moment the
legitimate client next refreshes (or vice versa: the legitimate client is
locked out and forced to re-authenticate, which is the safe failure mode),
without changing the access-token flow or the 90-day maximum session
lifetime.

Not in scope: persisting tokens outside process memory (see Known limits),
access-token issuance/verification, and a grace period for legitimate
same-token retries under network flakiness.

## Existing responsibilities searched

`src/auth/session.py` already owns refresh token issuance, validity checks,
and revocation, so rotation and reuse detection belong there rather than in a
new module. No other module imports these functions (verified by search), so
the signature changes are contained to this module and its tests.

## System and data flow

Login -> `issue_refresh_token` starts a token family with one absolute
expiry -> each refresh -> `rotate_refresh_token` retires the presented token
and mints its replacement in the same family -> a retired or revoked token
presented again -> `rotate_refresh_token` revokes the whole family.

## Decisions and trade-offs

See `docs/engineering/decisions/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`.

## Failure, security, and recovery

See `docs/engineering/security/rotating-refresh-tokens.md` for the threat
model. Rollback is reverting this module and its tests; no data migration is
involved since token state is in-memory.

## Verification evidence

Unit tests passed on 2026-07-26 against the session module and test changes
together (`.engineering/evidence/rotating-refresh-tokens.json`).

## Known limits and learning gaps

Token and revocation state live in a process-local dict/set, same as the
prior implementation. That doesn't survive a restart and doesn't work across
multiple server instances — a production deployment needs this backed by a
shared store (e.g. Redis or the primary database) before this can run behind
more than one process. There is also no grace period for a legitimate client
that retries a refresh call after a dropped response; that retry would look
identical to reuse and would revoke the session. Both are called out here
rather than silently shipped as if solved.

## References

- ADR: `docs/engineering/decisions/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`
- Threat model: `docs/engineering/security/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`

# 2026-07-26 · Rotating refresh tokens

Change ID: `rotating-refresh-tokens`
Created: `2026-07-26T10:00:00+00:00`
Status: Accepted

## Context

Refresh tokens were static for their full 90-day life and revocable only by
an operator who already knew a leak had happened. Nothing distinguished a
leaked token from a legitimate one at use time.

## Options considered

1. Keep static tokens, shorten the lifetime instead.
2. Rotate tokens on every use, extending the absolute expiry on each rotation
   (sliding session).
3. Rotate tokens on every use with one absolute expiry fixed at login, and
   revoke the whole family on reuse of a retired token.

## Decision

Choose option 3. Shortening the lifetime (option 1) reduces exposure but
doesn't detect theft — a leaked token is still fully usable until it expires.
A sliding expiry (option 2) detects reuse but lets an attacker who refreshes
first keep a session alive indefinitely, which defeats the point of an
absolute cap. Fixing the expiry at login (option 3) keeps the 90-day ceiling
meaningful while still detecting reuse, which is the standard OWASP
refresh-token-rotation pattern.

## Consequences and reversal

`is_refresh_valid` and `revoke` no longer take an `issued_at` argument — the
module now tracks issuance internally per token so it can enforce a
family-wide expiry. `rotate_refresh_token` is a new function; callers that
previously re-validated a static token on every request must switch to
calling it and handling `RefreshTokenExpired` / `RefreshTokenReused`.
Reversal is reverting `src/auth/session.py` and its tests; no stored data
needs migrating since state is in-memory.

## Implementation references

- `src/auth/session.py`

"""Login sessions.

Refresh tokens rotate on every use: exchanging one immediately retires it and
mints a replacement in the same token family. The family carries a single
absolute expiry set at login, so repeated silent refreshes cannot extend a
session past ``REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS``. Presenting a token that was already
retired (or whose family was revoked) can only happen if the token leaked and
someone raced the legitimate holder, so that attempt revokes the whole family
rather than just failing the one request.
"""

import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES = 15
REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS = 90


class RefreshTokenError(Exception):
    """Base class for refresh token failures."""


class RefreshTokenExpired(RefreshTokenError):
    """The token's family has passed its absolute expiry."""


class RefreshTokenReused(RefreshTokenError):
    """A retired or revoked token was presented again; its family is now revoked."""


@dataclass
class _Token:
    family_id: str
    family_expires_at: datetime
    active: bool = True


_TOKENS: dict[str, _Token] = {}
_REVOKED_FAMILIES: set[str] = set()


def issue_refresh_token(now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """Start a brand-new session family, e.g. at login."""
    moment = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    family_id = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    _TOKENS[token] = _Token(family_id=family_id, family_expires_at=refresh_expires_at(moment))
    return token


def refresh_expires_at(issued_at: datetime) -> datetime:
    return issued_at + timedelta(days=REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS)


def is_refresh_valid(token: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    moment = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    record = _TOKENS.get(token)
    if record is None or not record.active or record.family_id in _REVOKED_FAMILIES:
        return False
    return moment < record.family_expires_at


def rotate_refresh_token(token: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """Exchange a valid refresh token for its replacement.

    Raises ``RefreshTokenReused`` (and revokes the family) if ``token`` was
    already rotated away or its family was revoked. Raises
    ``RefreshTokenExpired`` if the family's absolute lifetime has elapsed.
    """
    moment = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    record = _TOKENS.get(token)
    if record is None:
        raise RefreshTokenReused("unknown refresh token")
    if not record.active or record.family_id in _REVOKED_FAMILIES:
        _REVOKED_FAMILIES.add(record.family_id)
        raise RefreshTokenReused("refresh token reuse detected; session revoked")
    if moment >= record.family_expires_at:
        raise RefreshTokenExpired("refresh token expired")

    record.active = False
    new_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    _TOKENS[new_token] = _Token(family_id=record.family_id, family_expires_at=record.family_expires_at)
    return new_token


def revoke(token: str) -> None:
    """Revoke a token's entire family, e.g. on logout."""
    record = _TOKENS.get(token)
    if record is not None:
        _REVOKED_FAMILIES.add(record.family_id)

import unittest
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from src.auth.session import (
    RefreshTokenExpired,
    RefreshTokenReused,
    is_refresh_valid,
    issue_refresh_token,
    revoke,
    rotate_refresh_token,
)


class SessionCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_fresh_token_is_valid(self):
        self.assertTrue(is_refresh_valid(issue_refresh_token()))

    def test_an_expired_token_is_rejected(self):
        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=91)
        token = issue_refresh_token(issued)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(token))

    def test_a_revoked_token_is_rejected(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        revoke(token)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(token))

    def test_rotating_returns_a_new_valid_token(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        new_token = rotate_refresh_token(token)
        self.assertNotEqual(token, new_token)
        self.assertTrue(is_refresh_valid(new_token))

    def test_rotating_retires_the_old_token(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        rotate_refresh_token(token)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(token))

    def test_reusing_a_rotated_token_is_rejected(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        rotate_refresh_token(token)
        with self.assertRaises(RefreshTokenReused):
            rotate_refresh_token(token)

    def test_reusing_a_rotated_token_revokes_the_whole_family(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        new_token = rotate_refresh_token(token)
        with self.assertRaises(RefreshTokenReused):
            rotate_refresh_token(token)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(new_token))

    def test_rotating_an_unknown_token_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(RefreshTokenReused):
            rotate_refresh_token("not-a-real-token")

    def test_rotating_an_expired_token_raises_expired(self):
        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=91)
        token = issue_refresh_token(issued)
        with self.assertRaises(RefreshTokenExpired):
            rotate_refresh_token(token)

    def test_rotation_preserves_the_familys_absolute_expiry(self):
        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=89)
        token = issue_refresh_token(issued)
        new_token = rotate_refresh_token(token)
        just_past_original_expiry = issued + timedelta(days=91)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(new_token, now=just_past_original_expiry))

    def test_revoking_any_family_member_blocks_the_current_token(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        new_token = rotate_refresh_token(token)
        revoke(token)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(new_token))
